title: Science & Nature 1

subtitle.text: Kayla groaned as she joined Kobe and Jenny at a table.
Kayla sighed. "I'm sick of making volcanoes explode."
Jenny made a face. "Mold is gross."
She ripped a sheet of paper from her notebook.
"Mr. Netter said we're supposed to work together, Kayla.
Kayla was folding wings on a paper airplane.
"We can measure how far it flies," Kayla said.
"Step one of the scientific method is to ask questions."
"How about, how does weight affect flight distance?" Kobe said.
"Next we have to come up with a hypothesis.
That's a guess about what will happen."
The kids did some research about airplane flight.
"Hmm," said Kayla. "I think a lighter plane will fly farther."
"That's our hypothesis: a light paper plane will fly farther."
"To test our hypothesis, we'll have to change the plane's weight."
"We can use these to add weight."
Kayla grabbed her airplane. "Let's find a runway!"
The kids went out into the hallway.
Kayla threw the plane and Kobe measured where it stopped.
"We should try to throw the plane the same way each time," said Jenny.
"So Kayla should keep flying the plane."
Kayla flew the plane several more times and Kobe measured each flight's distance.
Next they added two paperclips to the plane.
They flew and measured several more times.
"Let's try four paperclips now," Kayla said.
"Time to analyze our data!" Kobe said.
"Uh-oh." Jenny studied the results with a frown.
"Our plane flew farthest with two paperclips.
"Mr. Netter said a science experiment is for testing ideas.
Even if your hypothesis is incorrect, you still learn stuff."
Kayla grinned. "I learned something—science experiments [i@can@i] be fun!"
"Recycling is good for the earth," said Dad.
After breakfast Megan gathered food scraps.
She and Dad took them outside to the compost.
"Compost is good for the garden," said Dad.
Megan saw a strange box in the yard.
"You'll see later," said Dad with a wink.
"I'll get lunch ready here," said Dad.
At the store a clerk got some plastic bags.
"No thanks. We brought canvas shopping bags," said Mom.
Everyone was hungry after the long walk home.
"Awesome! The sun cooked the pizza," said Megan.
Speedy and Boomer were about to start their new job.
The two reindeer looked around the warehouse.
"I'm Rudolph," said a reindeer with a shiny red nose.
Our job tonight is to pull that sleigh through the air."
But our boss, Santa, has lots of stops to make.
We'll stop at millions of houses all over the world."
"Whoa!" Speedy gasped. "One night isn't enough time!"
Rudolph led Boomer and Speedy to a giant map.
"Earth is divided into 24 time zones," said Rudolph.
"Because there are 24 hours in one day?" asked Speedy.
"The sun only shines on one side of Earth at a time.@g]
So it's always daytime in some places and nighttime in others."
A big part of the map went dark.
"When it's 11:00 p.m. in Japan, it's only 11:00 a.m. in Argentina," Rudolph said.
"This is the International Date Line," said Rudolph.
We'll start at this line and fly west."@g]
"How long will we spend in each time zone?" asked Speedy.
"One hour. Then we'll move west to the next time zone," said Rudolph.
"Oh! The time will be one hour earlier there!" said Boomer.
We have 24 time zones to visit!"@g]
[g@"That's a lot of flying," said Boomer.
"Many children leave treats for us," said Rudolph.
"But watch out—the boss usually eats them all!"
Do you see that fire down there?
I'm going to jump down to it with my parachute!
No, I'm not doing it for fun.
I'm a special kind of firefighter called a smoke jumper.
Smoke jumpers are trained to fight fires in the wilderness.
During training we learn how to use parachutes.
We also learn different ways to fight fire.
Finally we focus on becoming stronger and fitter.
This helps us prepare for the dangerous work ahead.
When smoke jumpers get called to fight fire, we must act fast.
Airplanes carry us over the fire.
Then we jump down with our parachutes.
Planes drop our supplies, which include water, food, and fire-fighting tools.
We usually have everything we need for about three days.
Once we're on the ground, it's time to start fighting the fire.
Sometimes we spray water at the flames.
Helicopters also dump it from the air.
So we often have to try something else.
A fire line is a barrier that blocks fire.
You see, wildfires need fuel like dry trees and plants to keep burning.
So our goal is to destroy the fuel!
We start building the fire line by cutting down trees with chainsaws.
We even use fire to stop wildfire.
We burn smaller things like wood chips to clear the land.
The wildfire keeps spreading until it reaches our fire line.
Once it arrives, we hope our work pays off!
Without fuel, the wildfire should slow down or even die out.
Over time forests can get too crowded with plants and trees.
New plants can grow healthy and strong.
But sadly people cause more of them.
Sometimes campers forget to watch their campfires.
Or they don't completely put them out before leaving the forest.
The fire starts back up, and soon it's burning out of control.
Earth's weather is changing a lot.
Many places don't get enough rain, drying out forests and grasslands.
Because of this, wildfires are a growing problem.
Luckily smoke jumpers are trained to help.
It's a dangerous job, but I love it!
I travel all over, fighting wildfires.
It's time for me to jump. So long!
Hello! I'm Kat, and I'm a helicopter pilot.
Today I have an important mission.
A man was hiking in the mountains and got hurt.
I'm transporting rescue workers to the mountain to help him.
Climb aboard mine, and I'll tell you why.
It needs a long airstrip to take off and land.
They can lift straight up off the ground!
And they can land in places where an airplane can't land.
That makes them perfect for rescue missions like this one.
While we fly, I'll explain how helicopters work.
The main rotor sits on top of the helicopter.
I can control it with this lever.
Two long wings are attached to the rotor.
When the rotor spins, the blades spin too.
That makes the helicopter go up.
I can also control the tilt of the rotor blades.
By doing that, I can make the helicopter go in different directions.
My helicopter's second rotor is attached to the helicopter's tail.
It's smaller than the main one but just as important.
Here's why. The main rotor blades spin in one direction.
That makes the helicopter spin in the opposite direction.
So the tail rotor blades must spin too.
That keeps the helicopter steady, stopping it from spinning out of control.
Helicopters can't go as fast or as high as airplanes.
But they can go up and down, sideways and backward.
They can also move slowly over the land.
This will help us spot the hurt hiker.
Hmm. He's on a trail with a steep slope.
I don't see anywhere safe for me to land my helicopter.
But that's okay. I know what to do.
Unlike planes, helicopters can stay up in the air, in one spot.
I'll keep my helicopter right here.
A rescue worker can go down to help the hiker.
The rescue worker is back in the helicopter with the hiker.
Off we go to the hospital.
Do you see that big circle with an [i@H@i] on the roof?
I can gently land my helicopter on it.
I'm heading back to the airport!
Today I will grow an herb.
I push seeds in the dirt and cover them.
I whisper to my tray every day.
I run to Little Rosemary every day.
I water Little Rosemary every day.
I put her by the window.
I plant her in the garden.
I am glad Little Rosemary is here.
Seeds don't have feet or wings.
The wind helps this seed travel.
This is a willow tree seed.
The river helps this seed travel.
The bird helps this seed travel.
The bird's poop carries the seed to the ground.
The rain helps this seed fall to the ground.
"Look out! Get out of my way!"
This seed pops onto the ground.
This is a Spanish needles seed.
This seed sticks to the girl's sweater. "Ouch!"
Some seeds are really good travelers.
A lot of Samantha's friends wore glasses.
Henry's glasses made him look smart.
Glasses made shy Emma stand out.
Jenna had several pairs of glasses.
She liked her glasses to match her clothes!
Samantha wanted to look smarter and more stylish too.
"Do you have trouble seeing at school?" asked Mom.
"I'll make an appointment to see the optometrist," said Mom.
Samantha and Mom went to Dr. Green's office the next day.
She thought she could see fine.
Dr. Green asked Samantha to read a chart with rows of letters.
The letters at the bottom looked small and blurry.
Dr. Green sat down to talk to Samantha and Mom.
She wanted glasses, but she didn't want problems with her vision!
"Nearsighted people see things close up normally," said Dr. Green.
Dr. Green showed them a model of a round eyeball.
"The eyeball in nearsighted people is a little too long," he explained.
"In farsighted people the eyeball is too short."
"Is this because Samantha reads so much?" asked Mom.
"Too much reading doesn't cause the problem.
But it's good to take breaks to avoid eye strain or headaches," said Dr. Green.
"Being nearsighted can be caused by family history or the environment," Dr. Green continued.
"I heard eating carrots helps you see," said Samantha.
"Carrots and oily fish like salmon have vitamin A," said Dr. Green.
"So do dark leafy vegetables. Vitamin A helps keep eyes healthy."
"Will it fix my eyes?" asked Samantha.
"It won't cure your eyes." Dr. Green smiled.
"Spend more time outdoors in the sunshine.
Scientists believe that it slows children's eyes from becoming nearsighted.
For now, glasses will help you see clearly."
"Let me see how you look," said Mom.
She squinted and then leaned closer to Samantha.
"Wow! You do look good," said Mom.
"But maybe I need to make an appointment for myself!"
"Class, we're going to get a class pet," said Mrs. Frink.
"We need to decide what kind of pet."
"A dog is not a good class pet," said Mrs. Frink.
Mrs. Frink frowned. "Please be serious, Owen."
Mrs. Frink held up a hand.
"We'll each vote for the pet we want."
The teacher passed out pieces of paper for voting.
When everyone was done, Mrs. Frink collected the papers.
"Now we'll count the votes," she said.
Then we'll see which pet got the most votes."
Mrs. Frink drew a graph on the whiteboard.
"Let's write numbers along the left side of the graph," said Mrs. Frink.
"And let's write pets at the bottom of the graph."
Mrs. Frink read the first vote.
Alice wrote "hamster" at the bottom of the graph.
Then Mrs. Frink read another vote.
Alice added that to the graph.
Soon the bar graph was almost full.
"Boo!" said Alice. "Hamster got just one vote!"
"I see four votes for fish," said Pearl.
"Hedgehog got four votes too," said Eric.
"No, there's one more vote," said Mrs. Frink.
She colored one of the bars on the graph.
"I'm making your favorite food," said Mom.
Then he saw some spinach and carrots.
I'm just going to eat macaroni and cheese."
"You can't eat just that," said Mom.
"You need food from all five food groups."
"Macaroni and cheese has stuff from two food groups," said Theo.
"The macaroni is a grain, and the cheese is a dairy food.
Carrots have vitamin A," said Mom.
"Vitamin A is good for your eyes."
"Is salmon good for us?" asked Theo.
"Salmon is in the protein group," said Mom.
"So far dinner includes grains, vegetables, dairy, and protein.
But you said there are five food groups."
Just then Dad came in from the garden.
He had a basket of strawberries.
"The other group is fruits," Mom said.
"I'm still not sure about that salad," Theo said.
"When I grow up, I want to be an Arctic explorer."
"The Arctic is so cool!" said Ricky.
I want to see polar bears and Arctic foxes."
Ricky thought about it for a while.
"Is living in the Arctic very hard?" he asked.
"Did you know it's always light during summer?"
"And it's always dark during winter," said Dad.
"It gets very cold in the Arctic," Dad continued.
"Hot water can turn to ice right away!"
"It is not easy to live in the Arctic."
"I think I can do it," said Ricky.
"But I need to start training right away.
"All right. What can I do?" asked Dad.
"Can you add five dollars to my weekly allowance?" asked Ricky.
"I can buy ice cream with the money.@g]
That will help me get used to the cold!"
I planted red bell pepper seeds today.
First, I put the seeds in a pot.
Next, I covered them with soil.
This morning I checked the pepper pot.
Are roots growing in the soil?
Today I saw a green sprout!
A tiny stem is poking through the soil. Yay!
The stem gets taller each day.
This morning I planted the seedling in the backyard.
The sunny backyard is good for the plant.
Today I looked at my pepper plant.
I saw many small buds on it.
Flowers will grow from those buds.
Now flowers are blooming on the plant!
The tiny white flowers are so pretty.
But the plant has tiny green peppers!
All my peppers are red now.
I pick one and take a bite.
The visitor was Miss Santiago, the school nurse.@g]
The nurse smiled and shook her head.
"I'm here to talk about food allergies."
"My sister is allergic to tree nuts," said Jada.

Make sure everyone knows about your allergy.@g]

We say goodbye and run home.

Morning and evening star we view.
We live on it, you and me.
Named after the Roman god of war.
It looks blue and green to us.
The eight planets that we know.
Round and round the sun they go.
Hi! I'm Mac the apple tree.
I like spring because it's warm.
I have new flowers and leaves.
I like summer because it's hot.
I like autumn because it's cool.
I like winter because it's cold.
There are no kids outside at play.@g]
My tent and rope are stacked.@g]
The sun will shine its rays.@g]
[g@And the air will warm our hearts.
There'll be lots of games to start.@g]
The grass will be green and straight.@g]

The butterflies will dance and sway.@g]
I will ride my bike a long way.@g]

It makes me want to sing.@g]
But for now, I can only dream of spring.

Mr. Bird, what are you doing?"
I don't think you can fly."

I am a tiny water drop.
Whew! The sun is heating me up!
I am getting smaller and smaller.
Oh! I am going up, up, up into a cloud! Whee!
It is really cool up here.
I am getting bigger and bigger.
Oh no! I am too big and heavy!
I am falling from the sky!
Oh! I am in a river.
My friends are falling onto the ground.
They are seeping into the ground.
Now this river is moving fast!
We all need water to wash our hands and faces.
Mommy needs water to make lemonade.
Farmers need water to grow fruits and vegetables.
Dams need water to make electricity.
Firefighters need water to put out fires.
People need water to be healthy.
Water helps us in many ways.
So we need to keep our water clean.
